value.title: DMD R&D Headquarters
value.snippet: This retrofit included the conversion of existing core and shell space into a new 275,000-sq.-ft. headquarters for a confidential pharmaceutical client. The project scope includes lab space, open and closed office space, a gymnasium and all new electrical and mechanical systems. The new space served to consolidate the client’s existing lab and office spaces that were previously spread throughout the Greater Boston area, working to develop and commercialize the next generation of therapies for Duchenne’s Muscular Dystrophy.

value.title: GSK 200 Cambridgepark Drive Facility Expansion
value.snippet: This phased design-build project involved the expansion of GSK’s operations in 200 Cambridgepark Drive, adding 150,000-sq.-ft of cutting-edge lab, office and collaboration space. This expansion brings GSK scientists innovating new medicines and vaccines together under one roof for the first time, fostering collaboration and accelerating research in infectious diseases. DPR’s scope for this fast-track project included the demolition and construction of six floors in an occupied facility, transforming 85,000 sq. ft. of laboratories including ABSL and BSL spaces, 55,000 sq. ft. of open offices and collaboration rooms, and 4,000 sq. ft. of amenity/support areas. On-schedule turnover of floors was achieved through nine overlapping phases of construction, requiring meticulous planning and coordination to minimize disruption to ongoing research.

value.title: Exxon veteran Liam Mallon joins TMC board ahead of seabed mining push
value.snippet: The Metals Company said on Tuesday it has appointed former ExxonMobil upstream chief Liam Mallon to its board as the company advances plans to begin commercial recovery of polymetallic nodules in international waters under a US seabed mining framework. The move comes as the Trump administration signaled it is nearing approval for permits to mine the deep sea, part of a broader push to boost US access to the critical minerals used across much of the country's economy.

value.title: Unions at Antofagasta's Centinela copper mine ready for strike
value.snippet: The two main unions at Antofagasta Minerals' Centinela copper mine in Chile said on Tuesday they are ready to strike, but hope one can be averted if the company agrees to a deal during mandatory government-mediated talks. The unions, Minera Esperanza and Distrito Centinela, with 708 members combined, rejected the company's contract offer, triggering a five-day government mediation process that can be extended by mutual agreement.

value.title: Barrick CEO says North American IPO could slide into next January
value.snippet: Gold miner Barrick's proposed North American IPO could slide into January 2027, CEO Mark Hill said on Tuesday at the Mining Forum Americas in Colorado, adding that the company was on track to meet results guidance. Barrick still aims to launch the IPO by the end of this year, but it could be delayed because the company still needs to finish some formalities, Hill said.

value.title: Liontown lifts FY27 capex guidance by nearly 35% after approving lithium mine expansion
value.snippet: Liontown Resources on Wednesday approved an A$389-million ($271.68-million) expansion of its flagship Kathleen Valley lithium mine in Western Australia, prompting the company to raise its 2027 capital expenditure guidance by about 35%. The Perth-based lithium miner raised its 2027 total capital expenditure guidance to between A$435-million and A$495-million from between A$320-million and A$370-million previously.

value.title: Australia's Amplitude Energy approves FID for East Coast Supply Project
value.snippet: Australian gas producer Amplitude Energy said on Wednesday it had taken a final investment decision (FID) on the development phase of the East Coast Supply Project, which includes the construction of production infrastructure. The Adelaide-based company expects to spend A$190-million to A$210-million ($132.8-million to $146.7-million) on its share of the project's development over fiscal 2027 and 2028, with costs funded through existing cash reserves and operating cash flow.

value.title: Mintek roundtable highlights need to bridge research, industry gap
value.snippet: South Africa needs stronger collaboration between researchers, industry, government and other stakeholders to ensure scientific research is translated into commercially viable solutions for the mining industry and the broader economy, speakers said at the Mintek-Sci research roundtable, held on September 29 in Johannesburg. The need to strengthen this collaboration was a key theme highlighted at the first session of the research roundtable, titled “The Quadruple Helix in Science: Solving the Mineral Problems of the Future”, moderated by Mintek senior engineer Gertrude Marape.

value.title: Tungsten market value estimates vary, but the upward trajectory is clear
value.snippet: Research firm Market Data Forecast estimates the value of the global tungsten market to have been $5.14-billion in 2025, which will likely widen to $5.56-billion in 2026 and further to $10.45-billion by 2034. This equates to a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.2% between 2026 and 2034.

Sibanye-Stillwater will use the equipment at the Siphumelele shaft at its Rustenburg PGMs operations.

value.title: Akobo achieves best quarterly performance to date
value.snippet: Scandinavia-based gold producer Akobo Minerals has delivered its strongest quarter since production started at its Segele mine, in Ethiopia, with record gold production and earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) as well as considerable debt repayment, while continuing to invest in future growth. Gold production reached about 37 kg during the quarter ended June 30, the company’s highest quarterly production to date, at an average recovered grade of 38.5 g/t, which the company says is among the highest grades reported by any operating underground gold mine globally.

value.snippet: Video: 03:37:00 Watch the full replay of the launch of ESA’s state-of-the-art FLEX Earth Explorer satellite and the Copernicus Sentinel-3C satellite. Both were launched together aboard a Vega-C rocket from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana, marking a new milestone in Europe’s Earth Observation Programmes. Flight VV30 lifted off on 15 September at 03:21 (14 September at 22:21 local time). FLEX is designed to reveal a phenomenon invisible to the human eye: the faint fluorescence emitted by plants as they photosynthesise. Equipped with a Fluorescence Imaging Spectrometer, FLEX will detect and measure this incredibly weak signal from orbit. Because the fluorescence varies with plant health and environmental conditions, the measurements will provide scientists with new information about photosynthetic activity and vegetation stress on a global scale. value.snippet: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) are an invisible backbone for everyday life. They are essential for transportation, emergency response and public safety. value.snippet: Video: 00:04:46 ESA’s Civil Security from Space programme aims to save lives and livelihoods by reinforcing terrestrial systems that can become compromised by natural disasters or malicious actions. It aims to deliver a faster response than is presently possible by ensuring that real-time data is available anywhere through state-of-the-art space-enabled systems, making use of secure networks and reliable cloud computing to ensure the information is resilient and reliable. The programme also aims to enable governments and emergency services to act on an unfolding situation by using smart data gathering and intelligent processing to create a holistic awareness of the situation.

value.snippet: Image: Though the spiral galaxy in this new image by the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope seems serene, it hides a chaotic secret. This galaxy is NGC 4698, and it lies about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. It’s one of over one thousand galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, the nearest large cluster of galaxies bound together by gravity. As a spiral galaxy similar to our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disc of stars, gas and dust. Its centre is dominated by a galactic bulge. The diffuse off-white glow of the galaxy’s bulge comes from stars smaller, older, and cooler than the massive blue stars that dot the galaxy’s outer disc. These tightly packed stars orbit a supermassive black hole containing millions of times the Sun’s mass. Scientists have found signs that this black hole is actively growing, drawing gas inward with its gravitational pull. value.title: Hubble's superbubble scene
value.snippet: Image: This sprawling cosmic vista and subject of today’s ESA/Hubble Picture of the Month comes from the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). The LMC is the largest of the small galaxies that orbit our Milky Way galaxy . At just 160 000 light-years away, the LMC offers a close look at highly active stellar birthsites like the nebula shown here. This nebula is named LHA 120-N44, or N44 for short, and it’s located in the constellation Dorado. The appearance of this photogenic nebula is dominated by two features: a vast central void and a shell of dense, dusty gas. The central void is a ‘superbubble’ spanning roughly 210 by 140 light-years. The glittering stars at the centre of the void are responsible for its creation; through their powerful stellar winds and explosive supernovae , these stars have expelled much of the gas from which they were born. value.snippet: Video: 00:02:57 Is there life on Terran V? Join the adventure to the fictional planet and find out what it takes to reach the farthest frontiers of deep space. This video uses a fictional spacecraft and a fictional star system to illustrate a gravity assist manoeuvre – also known as a planetary flyby or swingby. The gravity assist is one of the most important techniques in deep-space navigation. By carefully passing close to a planet, a spacecraft can exchange orbital momentum with the much larger body. From the spacecraft’s perspective, this results in a change in trajectory and a significant boost (or reduction) in speed relative to the star at the centre of the system, without needing to use much fuel. While the Terran system may be fictional, the physics behind gravity assists is very real. value.snippet: Video: 00:02:27 2025 marks a landmark year for Europe’s ‘bridge between Earth and space’. The European Space Agency’s Estrack satellite tracking network turns 50 . Since its inception in 1975, Estrack – ESA’s global network of ground stations – has formed the vital communication bridge between satellites in orbit and mission control at the European Space Operations Centre (ESOC) in Darmstadt, Germany. Now comprising six stations spanning six countries, Estrack has grown into a strategic asset for Europe, enabling communication with spacecraft, transmitting commands and receiving scientific data. The network keeps an eye on satellites no matter their location: tracking them across Earth orbit, voyaging to comets or asteroids, keeping station at the scientifically important Sun-Earth Lagrange points, and deep into our Solar System. value.snippet: What are crack spreads and why are they elevated? Crack spreads are indicators of the profitability of refining crude oil into petroleum products such as gasoline and diesel. One common crack spread is calculated by subtracting the spot market price of a gallon of crude oil from the wholesale price of a gallon of refined product. Since May, the gasoline crack spread in New York Harbor has averaged about $1 per gallon (gal) higher than in 2025, when the crack spread peaked around 60 cents/gal. Gasoline crack spreads are elevated primarily because of tight gasoline supplies globally.

value.title: Digital Realty | FRA29 Data Center

All data suites are supported with resilient power and cooling infrastructure with a total of 10 backup generators. A green roof system is a unique feature of this project within the campus. value.snippet: Video: 00:00:48 On 28 September 2026, ESA’s Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer ( Juice ) successfully completed a gravity assist flyby of Earth. Flight controllers guided the spacecraft close to our home planet to increase its velocity by 3.5 km/s and deflect its trajectory by an angle of 20°. As Juice flew just 8640 km above the Indian Ocean, it snapped a series of images with its onboard monitoring cameras, giving us a unique ‘Juice eye view’ of our home planet. Juice’s monitoring cameras provide 1024 x 1024 pixel snapshots that can be processed in colour. Their main purpose is to monitor the spacecraft’s various booms and antennas, especially during the challenging period after launch. The photos they captured of Earth during the flyby are a bonus. In the first seconds of the video we see a view from Juice monitoring camera 2 – or JMC2 – with Earth appearing as a thin crescent at the bottom right of the frame. The agreement provides for De Beers to assume full ownership of the Gahcho Kué diamond mine in the Northwest Territories, releases the Mountain Province entities from associated obligations and liabilities, and preserves rights that allow the company to regain an ownership interest in the mine in future.

value.title: Nordic business alliance weighs expanding into critical minerals
value.snippet: Nordic Compass, a competitiveness-focused business alliance, is considering branching out into critical raw materials to build up the region’s capacity to process minerals needed by European industry. The network involving of some of the region’s biggest companies and investors is mapping out concrete actions across capital markets, deep technology, defence and energy, and is now considering adding a fifth work stream, according to its chairman, Jyrki Katainen, a former Finnish PM.

value.title: Osmond Resources study confirms potential for EU's first rare earths, zircon, titanium mine
value.snippet: ASX-listed Osmond Resources has published a scoping study advancing the case for the EU's first rare earths, zircon and titanium mine. The scoping study for Osmond's Orión project, in Jaén province, Andalucía, Spain, confirms a low capital expenditure requirement of $299-million, an after-tax net present value of $2.31-billion, an internal rate of return of 145% and a payback period of six months.

value.title: Algoma advises of 65% third-quarter shipment drop from unplanned outage

value.snippet: Video: 00:08:40 For ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot, her first steps into space were only the beginning. In less than 15 days, she performed three extravehicular activities, or EVAs, spending 19 hours and 42 minutes outside the International Space Station. Across three demanding spacewalks, Sophie and her crewmates replaced critical Station hardware, installed a new communications antenna, carried out maintenance, and prepared experiments for future work, all while adapting to the challenges of working in the extreme environment of space. From her very first spacewalk to leading her third as EV1, Sophie demonstrated what it takes to work beyond Earth: technical skill, perseverance, adaptability, and trust in the teams supporting you.

value.title: ESTEC, ESA’s technical heart, seen from orbit
value.snippet: Image: From the International Space Station, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot has photographed cities, coastlines and landscapes across the world during her nearly eight-month εpsilon mission. This time, her camera turned towards a place with a particularly familiar connection: ESA’s European Space Research and Technology Centre (ESTEC) in Noordwijk, the Netherlands. ESTEC is ESA’s largest establishment and its technical heart, where many European space projects take shape. Its work spans science, Earth observation and human exploration, including ESA’s European Service Module, which powers and propels Orion on Artemis missions to the Moon and is monitored from ESTEC by European engineers. For astronauts, looking back at Earth is not only an opportunity to admire our planet from a unique perspective. Taking photographs can also be a way of reconnecting with familiar places and with the people working below. For Sophie, sharing this image is a nod to the ESA colleagues who have supported her

value.title: Research, innovation key to unlocking greater critical minerals value, conference hears
value.snippet: Greater investment in research, innovation and collaboration by academia and industry is needed to unlock more value from Africa’s critical mineral resources, Stellenbosch University chemical engineering associate professor and African Rainbow Minerals (ARM) geometallurgical research chair Margreth Tadie said at the Mintek-Sci 2026 conference, in Johannesburg, on October 2. In her keynote address focused on critical minerals, she said South Africa and the broader African continent had significant mineral resources but needed to strengthen the ability to process and add value to those resources.

value.title: AfDB, German Ministry partner to develop Africa railway systems' regional integration
value.snippet: Development finance institution the African Development Bank (AfDB) Group and the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) have formed a partnership to develop Africa’s railway systems and deepen regional economic integration. The two entities will collaborate to reduce Africa’s transport costs, improve cross-border interoperability, promote low-carbon transport solutions and promote and embed sustainable transport policies.

value.title: Skeleton Coast Uranium completes digitisation of historical Namibia exploration data
value.snippet: TSX-V-listed Skeleton Coast Uranium Corp has informed shareholders that metals and mining advisory firm Practara has completed the digitisation of the historical exploration data for Skeleton Coast's five exclusive prospecting licences (EPLs) in the Erongo region of Namibia. This completes the Phase 1 data consolidation and target definition recommended in Skeleton Coast's technical reports. Interpretation of the compiled data has defined priority target areas on each licence for field validation.

value.title: Glencore secures RIGI benefits for MARA project in Argentina
value.snippet: Diversified miner Glencore has received approval for the Minera Agua Rica – Alumbrera (MARA) project under Argentina’s Incentive Regime for Large Investments (RIGI). RIGI is a national legal framework to attract multimillion-dollar investments through a 30-year guarantee of tax, customs, and regulatory stability.

value.title: Sovereign director steps down
value.snippet: Rutile and graphite miner Sovereign Metals, which is developing the Kasiya project, in Malawi, has announced the resignation of nonexecutive director and former MD Dr Julian Stephens. Stephens was MD of the company from June 2016 to October 2023. During that time, he was instrumental in the company's growth and development. He first identified rutile mineralisation in Malawi and subsequently led the team that discovered Sovereign's world-class Kasiya deposit, progressing the project through its scoping and prefeasibility study stages.

value.title: Indonesia launches pilot commodity export monitoring platform
value.snippet: Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia, a company established by the Indonesian government to supervise commodity exports, has started the test phase for a new monitoring platform aimed at boosting price transparency, the firm said in a statement. The firm, also known as DSI, launched the pilot phase of its National Data Intelligence (NADI) platform on Thursday, which will be responsible for supervising exports of major commodities.

value.title: Vacuuming the ventilation grids in Columbus
value.snippet: Video: 00:01:00 This video was published on social media by ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot with the following caption: [ version FR ] Day 222, orbit 3442 — More vacuum cleaning in space! Keeping the ventilation grids clean is essential in an environment like ours, where the air is continuously recycled in a near-closed-loop system. Much like on a submarine, or a climate-controlled laboratory, clean airflow isn't just a matter of comfort, it's an important part of keeping both the crew and the Station running smoothly. value.title: Premier African Minerals to raise £1.2m for Zimbabwe project
value.snippet: London-listed Premier African Minerals has completed a subscription to raise about £1.2-million before expenses through the issue of 27.52-billion new ordinary shares of nil par value in the capital of the company at an issue price of 0.00436p per new ordinary share. The net proceeds will provide additional working capital to support the planned restart of operations at the Zulu lithium and tantalum project, in Zimbabwe, including the potential remobilisation of mining activities and restart of the processing plant.

value.title: Sasol tops emerging market peers on oil-from-coal bonanza
value.snippet: This year’s oil price rally has produced one clear winner: South Africa’s Sasol is the top-performing emerging-market stock outside Asia and many analysts are betting its bull run has further to go. Sasol has handed investors dollar a return of almost 120% this year, building on last year’s 45% gain and putting it on track for its best annual performance since at least 1991. That’s not far behind Asia’s giant chip and internet companies in MSCI’s main emerging-equity index.

value.title: Founders Factory, Rio Tinto select five latest startups for Mining Tech Accelerator

value.title: Gold retains key reserve status despite surging bond yields, central bankers say
value.snippet: Gold remains a strategic reserve asset as concerns over rising government debt and geopolitical instability boost its appeal as a haven from risk, two central bankers said on Monday, even after this year's surge in bond yields. Gold prices typically retreat as yields rise, boosting the opportunity cost of holding non-interest bearing assets.

This marks more than a decade of quarterly monitoring that brings together communities, academics, journalists, community leaders, authorities and other stakeholders to observe and take part directly in environmental monitoring around the operation.

value.title: Gemcorp joins Madagascar to raise $5bn for energy, mining

The partnership was unveiled late last month as a key pillar of the new government’s efforts to drive economic growth in one of the world’s poorest countries. The London-headquartered firm intends to set up an office in the capital city, Antananarivo, before the end of the year.

value.title: Latest Lithium Ridge drilling highlights upside potential

value.title: Greenland Mines increases ownership in anorthosite producer AnorTech to 19.9%

Greenland Mines considers Gronne Bjerg a potential source of feedstock for US smelter-grade and high-purity alumina production in a market where net imports met an estimated 71% of US alumina consumption in 2025.

value.title: Alurion confirms direct road haul viability for Amargosa bauxite shipments

value.title: Congo launches geological survey in push to unlock mineral potential
value.snippet: Democratic Republic of Congo has launched a nationwide airborne geological mapping programme aimed at improving knowledge of its vast mineral reserves to reduce exploration risk and attract investment into underexplored regions, its geological agency said. Congo is the world's largest cobalt producer and Africa's top copper producer, but authorities say less than 10% of the country's territory has been thoroughly explored.

value.title: PwC sees opportunities for mining to bolster benefits following stronger performance
value.snippet: South Africa’s mining sector entered this year on a stronger footing, underpinned by higher platinum group metals (PGM) and gold prices, improved mineral reserve positions and growing interest in critical minerals, professional services firm PwC’s ‘SA Mine 2026’ report shows. Presenting key findings from the report, PwC Africa Energy, Utilities and Resources leader Andries Rossouw said the sector achieved considerable growth in revenue, profitability, free cash flow and market capitalisation.

value.title: Saldanha Iron Ore Terminal undergoes scheduled maintenance programme
value.snippet: State-owned freight transport and logistics company Transnet has announced that the Saldanha Iron Ore Terminal (IOT) has begun its yearly maintenance shutdown, which will run for 16 days from October 6 to 21. As part of its ‘Reinvent for Growth’ strategy, the maintenance shutdown at this terminal will focus on infrastructure upgrades, dust management systems, and the refurbishment of key mechanical and electrical components across the terminal’s cargo-handling equipment.
